capabilities: Detect encodings via create/rename events plus startup and periodic scans
Convert UTF-16, UTF-8 BOM, and EUC-KR/CP949 files to UTF-8
Wait for sync writes to finish before reading files
Leave already-clean or unidentifiable files untouched with a warning
Convert the current file or scan the whole vault via commands
disambiguation: Not a text formatter; it only converts file character encoding and changes nothing else in file contents.
extras: Already-corrupted files cannot be recovered; the plugin must be installed on every device that adds files since .obsidian/plugins/ is not always synced. A beta version is available via BRAT, and the README includes a full Korean-language section.
motivation: The author lost a meeting transcript: a UTF-16 .txt synced through Self-hosted LiveSync was blocked as corrupted, and force-receiving it turned every Korean character into . They built the plugin so importing files 'just works'.
problem: Obsidian assumes every note is UTF-8, so text files in other encodings get permanently corrupted ( or mojibake) the moment Obsidian or a sync plugin touches them.

relations.evidence: With a sync plugin like Self-hosted LiveSync, the damage gets worse
handles the temp-file-then-rename pattern used by Resilio, Dropbox, and friends
BRAT → Add beta plugin → enter kathar0s/obsidian-encoding-autofix

summary: Encoding converter that detects non-UTF-8 text files (UTF-16, UTF-8 BOM, EUC-KR/CP949) added to the vault and rewrites them as clean UTF-8.
